title: Intelligence Briefing Dashboard
subtitle: Weekly Conflict Monitor · All Regions
sources: Reuters · AP News · Al Jazeera · ACLED · US Embassy Alerts · LiveUAMap · BNO News · ISW · British Defence Intelligence · Kyiv Post · Sudan Tribune · Irrawaddy · CNN · NBC · CBS · Fox News · HRW · UN News · CFR · Times of Israel · NPR · CNBC · Atlantic Council · Sudan Tribune · US State Dept · OHCHR · Wikipedia · Washington Post · Amnesty International · AEI · Moscow Times · Kyiv Independent

regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Gulf oil-war threshold has been crossed — Houthi strikes moved from shipping interdiction to direct attacks on core Saudi Aramco refining infrastructure at Jizan and Yanbu (25 Jul), the first such strikes since 2022, pushing Brent crude above $100/barrel and materially raising the odds of a distinct Saudi-Houthi military confrontation layered atop the US-Iran war.

A fragile US-Iran pause emerged after the war's most intense stretch — following 13 consecutive nights of US strikes and Iranian tanker attacks that collapsed Hormuz traffic, both sides held fire for three consecutive days (25-27 Jul) amid Qatar/Pakistan-mediated talks, the first genuine de-escalation signal in weeks.

Israel's containment lines are fraying on two fronts simultaneously — the 24 Jul al-Tal killings triggered the worst West Bank escalation yet, with HRW warning of mass-atrocity risk, even as Lebanon strikes intensified rather than eased, prompting both Lebanon and Jordan to be re-escalated to CRITICAL this week.

Iran-aligned proxy and insurgent networks are exploiting the wider war's bandwidth constraints — Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah is openly defying the 30 Sep disarmament deadline, Syria's ISIL cells sustain a steady tempo with Aleppo as a new front, and Jordan has shifted from an interception zone to a directly targeted state.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 22 Jul — Gaza-wide: The UN human rights office condemned Israeli strikes over the preceding week that killed at least 57 Palestinians, including 6 children.
24 Jul — Gaza: Israel issued fresh displacement orders for several areas, then struck the territory, killing at least 2 Palestinians.
26 Jul — Deir al-Balah: An Israeli air strike hit a vehicle, killing 2 Hamas security officials, including the head of Hamas's internal security service in central Gaza.
27 Jul — Gaza-wide: The cumulative death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire reached 1,203 Palestinians killed, up from 1,092 the previous week.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Strike tempo and the cumulative death toll both rose week-on-week, showing the nominal ceasefire continuing to erode. Absent a genuine disarmament/governance breakthrough, expect continued high-tempo strikes calibrated below full re-invasion threshold, with the toll likely crossing 1,300-1,500 within 90 days.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 23 Jul — Southern Lebanon: An Israeli drone strike wounded paramedics amid escalating operations despite the withdrawal framework.
28 Jul — Nabatieh al-Fawqa: Israeli drones struck an apartment complex, causing substantial damage and fire, part of near-daily strikes continuing through the week.
Ongoing through 28 Jul — Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh: Lebanese Army deployment into the 'pilot zone' villages proceeded only slowly as Israeli strikes continued elsewhere.
Cumulative — Nationwide: Lebanese health authorities report at least 4,303 killed and 12,202 injured by Israeli attacks since March 2026, with 1.6 million+ displaced.
countries.coa: Upgraded back to CRITICAL from HIGH. The withdrawal framework is proving largely symbolic on the ground — Israeli strikes persisted at a pace inconsistent with genuine de-escalation, including a notable 28 July strike on an apartment complex and paramedics wounded on 23 July, undercutting last week's downgrade rationale. Expect continued drone strikes on south Lebanon targeting alleged Hezbollah infrastructure, punctuated by incidents affecting civilians and medical responders, while Lebanese Army deployment into pilot zones remains slow and largely cosmetic absent a verifiable halt in Israeli strikes.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 20-24 Jul — Nationwide: US strikes continued for a 13th consecutive night before pausing; Iran's Health Ministry reported at least 50 killed and 500+ wounded in this phase.

22-23 Jul — Strait of Hormuz/Omani waters: Iran struck and disabled two 'rogue' supertankers and hit two tankers in Omani waters; Hormuz commercial traffic collapsed to fewer than 10 vessels per day from roughly 100.
25-27 Jul — Nationwide: The US and Iran maintained a mutual pause in strikes for a third consecutive day amid Qatar- and Pakistan-mediated talks; Iran denied agreeing to a 10-day ceasefire.
27 Jul — Nationwide: The war's cumulative cost was estimated at $40-113 billion depending on source, sharply up from $37.5bn a week earlier.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, but a fragile pause has emerged. After 13 consecutive nights of strikes and Iranian tanker attacks that collapsed Hormuz shipping, both sides held fire for three consecutive days (25-27 Jul) amid Qatar/Pakistan-mediated talks — the first genuine de-escalation signal in weeks, though the war's pattern of repeated ceasefire collapses urges caution. Expect either a formalized interim ceasefire within 1-2 weeks or renewed strikes if Iran conducts further tanker/Hormuz attacks or US forces sustain casualties; regional spillover into Jordan, Syria, Iraq and the Gulf will track directly with the strike tempo.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 22 Jul — Red Sea: Houthis claimed strikes on two Saudi oil tankers, Encelia and Layla, for allegedly violating the blockade; at least 7 vessels diverted from Bab el-Mandeb.
23 Jul — Red Sea: Houthis claimed additional strikes on two more Saudi oil tankers amid the wider Iran-linked escalation.
25 Jul — Jizan/Yanbu, Saudi Arabia: Houthis struck Aramco refineries directly for the first time since 2022, sparking a fire at Jizan; Brent crude surged above $100/barrel.
Ongoing — Hodeidah governorate: Renewed clashes between government-aligned forces and Houthi forces continued near the west coast supply corridor.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, escalation confirmed and accelerating. Houthi operations moved from shipping interdiction to direct strikes on core Saudi oil infrastructure within a week — a significant threshold crossing. Expect continued and possibly expanded strikes on Red Sea coast refineries and export terminals, sustained blockade enforcement, and continued oil-market volatility, raising the likelihood of a direct Saudi-Houthi military confrontation distinct from the US-Iran track.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 24 Jul — Al-Tal village, near Nablus: A settler attack on Palestinian homes triggered a shootout that killed 4 Palestinians and 2 Israelis, the deadliest single settler-related incident of the current wave.

24-25 Jul — West Bank-wide: Following the al-Tal killings, Israel launched a major counterterrorism operation; Army Radio counted roughly 30 separate settler attacks across the territory over the following weekend.
25-26 Jul — West Bank-wide: Israeli forces conducted mass arrests of Palestinians as Human Rights Watch warned of a 'surge in settler violence threatening mass atrocities.'
26 Jul — Tel Aviv: Nine people were arrested at a protest against West Bank settler violence.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The al-Tal killings mark a sharp escalatory inflection in West Bank settler violence, triggering both settler reprisals and an Israeli military crackdown that risks further radicalizing the situation, layered atop Israel's continued direct combatant role in the Iran war and near-daily Gaza strikes. Expect sustained high-tempo settler attacks and IDF mass-detention operations without near-term policy correction; risk of a mass-casualty inter-communal incident within the West Bank is elevated over the next 90 days.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 24 Jul — Erbil: Air defenses intercepted and destroyed 5 explosive-laden drones targeting the vicinity of Erbil International Airport, which hosts US-led coalition forces; attribution remains contested between Iranian forces and Iran-backed militias.

Ongoing through 28 Jul — Nationwide: Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba publicly reaffirmed refusal to disarm, linking compliance to withdrawal of coalition forces ahead of the 30 Sep deadline.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Iraq remains a secondary front of the US-Iran war, with Iran-aligned militias using deniable drone attacks against coalition infrastructure at Erbil as leverage. The 30 September disarmament deadline is set to become a flashpoint given Kataib Hezbollah's public rejection; expect continued intermittent drone/rocket incidents against Erbil with attribution likely to remain contested.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 22 Jul — Red Sea: Houthis claimed strikes on tankers Encelia and Layla; Encelia was confirmed hit.
23 Jul — Red Sea: Additional Houthi strikes were claimed on two more Saudi oil tankers.

25 Jul — Jizan/Yanbu: Houthi missile and drone strikes hit Aramco refineries directly — the first such attack since 2022; a fire broke out at Jizan, confirmed by satellite imagery, and Brent crude spiked above $100/barrel.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained; this week's Aramco refinery strikes confirm last week's upgrade. Saudi Arabia has moved from an indirect, shipping-interdiction threat environment to direct kinetic strikes on its oil export infrastructure for the first time since 2022. Expect continued and potentially expanded Houthi targeting of Red Sea coast refineries and terminals, sustained blockade enforcement, and a significantly raised probability of direct Saudi military retaliation against Houthi positions in Yemen.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: Through Jul — Nationwide: The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights documented 5 ISIL attacks in July, with Aleppo emerging as a new front (12 events in 2026, up from near-zero prior).
Ongoing — Nationwide: 52 ISIL attacks on government forces have been recorded in 2026, versus 16 for all of 2025.
Ongoing through 28 Jul — Nationwide: Syria retained a neutral posture in the Iran war but continued to suffer damage from Iranian missiles intercepted over its territory by Israel.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Syria's security picture remains defined by two parallel threats: a resurgent ISIL insurgency, with Aleppo as a notable new front, sustaining a steady tempo of attacks against security forces, and continued exposure as a transit/intercept zone for the wider Iran-Israel-US missile war. Expect continued small-cell ISIL attacks testing the new government's stretched security capacity, alongside incidental damage from intercepted missiles absent a ceasefire in the Iran war.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 15 Jul — Suez Canal-wide: The Suez Canal Authority implemented its first major surcharge revision in 3 years — loaded tanker surcharges rose from 25% to 37%, dry bulk more than doubled to 22%, and container ships now face a 12% surcharge.
Ongoing — Suez Canal: Transit volumes remain roughly 60% below pre-Red Sea-crisis levels, with carriers using selective, risk-assessed routing.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Egypt's exposure remains primarily economic rather than kinetic; the July 15 surcharge hikes reflect the Canal Authority's effort to recoup revenue amid persistently depressed transit volumes, itself now compounded by the Houthi blockade and Aramco strikes further destabilizing regional shipping confidence. Sinai security risk remains a standing, low-tempo condition rather than an escalating one this week.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 22 Jul — Aqaba: Missile alert sirens sounded as Jordanian forces intercepted 4 Iranian missiles and 4 drones, with 2 further missiles falling in uninhabited areas, coinciding with collapsed ceasefire talks.
Ongoing — Aqaba: The IRGC claimed the strikes specifically targeted US-linked assets at Aqaba airport, alongside Kuwait- and Syria-based US assets, as part of the same regional wave.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. Confirmed direct Iranian missile and drone attacks specifically targeting Aqaba on 22 July mark a step up from near-daily interception of transiting fire to direct targeting of Jordanian territory. Expect continued missile/drone activity against Aqaba as long as the US-Iran war continues, with elevated risk to the port, airport and adjacent Eilat from interception debris; a sustained ceasefire would likely reduce this risk quickly, while renewed US strikes would likely trigger renewed Iranian targeting of Jordan within days.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 26 Jul — Benghazi: Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar met with Zintan tribal leaders, continuing political consolidation tied to the Boulos unification initiative.

27 Jul — Tripoli: Protests over prolonged power cuts (up to 10 hours/day) spread across multiple districts, including road blockades on the coastal road in Janzour, as load-shedding resumed after two years of relative stability.
Ongoing — Tripoli: Rival militias were reported massing amid ideological rifts, raising fears of renewed clashes, though no armed clash was confirmed this week.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Libya's near-term risk picture is shifting from purely factional toward socioeconomic: worsening power cuts are driving civil unrest in Tripoli that could be exploited by rival armed factions already reported massing in the capital. The Haftar-GNU unification track continues to show genuine momentum, but militia buildup and unresolved Misrata-aligned opposition remain a latent trigger for renewed clashes.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 4 Jul — Tunis: Ennahda Secretary-General Ajmi Ourimi and member Mosaab Gharbi were each sentenced to 3 years on terrorism-related charges.

8 Jul — Tunis: 21 people, including Ennahda leaders and former officials, were sentenced to 12-35 years in the 'Conspiracy 2' case, with Rached Ghannouchi receiving an additional 14-year sentence in absentia.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No new dated incidents were identified this week; the opposition crackdown appears to have reached a plateau following the 4-8 July sentencing wave. Expect continued international human rights criticism without near-term policy reversal, and continued monitoring for appeals processes or potential unrest triggered by the sentences.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Ukraine's political-military crisis outlived its 24 July deadline — Zelensky's partial concession of dismissing Syrskyi failed to satisfy protesters, who rejected Fedorov's alternative posts and expanded demands; protests hit an 11th consecutive day by 26 Jul, running in parallel with continued mass-casualty Russian strikes including the 24 Jul Bucha arms-expo strike that killed 10.

Russia's fuel and refinery crisis is deepening — Ukrainian strikes on the Afipsky and Salavat refineries and a Novorossiysk state of emergency compound rationing already reported in 78+ Russian regions.

The South Caucasus is bifurcating further — Georgia's crackdown intensified past Day 600 of protests, Armenia absorbed a fresh Russian trade strike tied to its EU pivot, while Azerbaijan deepened Western energy ties even as it keeps threatening to leave the Council of Europe.

Belarus and Moldova show a rising but still low-intensity hybrid-pressure pattern — Moldova's new pro-EU government immediately drew Russian diplomatic friction, while Belarus combines Ukraine-border military buildup with a renewed migrant-pressure campaign against Latvia ahead of its October elections.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 21 Jul — Kyiv: Zelensky dismissed Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi and appointed Joint Forces Commander Mykhailo Drapatyi, a partial concession to protesters that did not reinstate Fedorov.
23 Jul — Kyiv: Fedorov rejected Zelensky's alternative posts, stating he will accept 'no position other than minister of defence,' entrenching the political standoff.
24 Jul — Bucha, Kyiv Oblast: A Russian ballistic missile struck a defense-industry exhibition, killing at least 10 and injuring 100+; Russia's MoD claimed it deliberately targeted the event.

26 Jul — Kyiv/Chernihiv: Russia launched 7 ballistic missiles and 136 drones overnight; a drone hit a Chernihiv supermarket, killing 2 including a child, as protests over Fedorov's dismissal reached an 11th consecutive day.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, compounding. The 24 July deadline passed without resolution — the leadership rift is now a three-week standoff running in parallel with, not resolved by, continued mass-casualty Russian strikes. Expect the Fedorov standoff to persist as low-boil civil unrest given Zelensky's calculated partial concessions, while Russia sustains large-scale missile/drone salvos against Kyiv and defense-industrial targets and Ukraine continues its long-range campaign against Russian refining capacity.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 14 Jul — Bashkortostan: Ukrainian drones struck the Neftekhim Salavat facility, one of Russia's largest petrochemical plants.
26 Jul — Krasnodar Krai: Fresh drone strikes hit the Afipsky refinery and a military unit; a local state of emergency was declared in Novorossiysk, a key crude-export gateway.
26-27 Jul — Nationwide: Russia launched 147 drones against Ukraine overnight while Ukraine continued its long-range strike campaign against Russian export and oil infrastructure.
Ongoing — Nationwide: Fuel rationing continues, with petrol shortages now reported in at least 78 regions including occupied Crimea.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect Ukraine to sustain or intensify strikes on refining and export infrastructure — the Krasnodar, Novorossiysk and Bashkortostan pattern suggests a deliberate effort to hit both domestic refining and export-earning nodes — pushing fuel rationing into more regions through Q3. Domestic unrest risk from fuel shortages remains a slow-burn variable rather than acute.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: Ongoing — Brest/border zone: Lukashenko confirmed dispersal of Special Operations Forces along the Ukraine border, framed as defensive, amid continued construction of roads and ammunition/fuel storage sites near the frontier.

Ongoing — Latvia border: A renewed migrant-pressure campaign saw Latvia record 111 attempted illegal crossings from Belarus in a single day, with allegations Belarusian security forces are escorting and equipping migrants ahead of Latvia's October elections.
25 Jul — Ukraine-Belarus border: Ukraine continued fortifying its 1,084km border with Belarus with anti-drone netting, minefields and closed crossings, citing the ongoing Belarusian military buildup.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Expect Belarus to continue leaning on hybrid levers — border militarization paired with migration pressure against the Baltics — as a low-cost way to tie down NATO attention ahead of Latvia's October elections, rather than direct involvement in the Ukraine war.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 21 Jul — Chișinău: Parliament confirmed the Tofan government (53-21); PM Tofan outlined a goal of signing an EU accession agreement by 2028 and full membership by 2030.
22 Jul — Chișinău/Moscow: Russia summoned Moldova's ambassador, alleging Moldovan security forces 'threatened and pressured' Russian embassy staff, and warned of 'symmetrical' retaliatory measures.
23 Jul — Chișinău: Moldova's Foreign Ministry warned citizens against non-essential travel to Russia and Belarus, citing reports of Russia pressuring Moldovan nationals to sign military contracts.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Expect the Tofan government's EU-accession push to continue drawing retaliatory friction from Moscow — likely further diplomatic incidents, disinformation and pressure on Moldovan citizens in Russia — rather than renewed airspace violations in the near term.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 22 Jul — Tbilisi: TV Formula journalist Vakho Sanaia was jailed for 14 days over Facebook posts satirizing the parliament speaker; comedian Onise Okriashvili was attacked by unidentified men hours later.
26 Jul — Tbilisi: Police detained 10 protesters on the 606th consecutive day of protests for carrying signs criticizing Bidzina Ivanishvili.
27 Jul — Tbilisi: An activist was detained on the 607th day of protests, again over an Ivanishvili-related poster.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect the government to continue incremental judicial harassment of journalists, comedians and protest figures rather than a single dramatic crackdown, sustaining the daily-protest equilibrium past its 600-day mark.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 24-27 Jul — Moscow/Yerevan: Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor announced a restriction on dairy imports from all Armenian enterprises effective 27 July, the latest in a string of Russian bans widely seen as political leverage tied to Armenia's EU/US pivot.
Ongoing — Yerevan: Pro-Russian oligarch Samvel Karapetyan, facing coup-plot charges, publicly claimed to have a 'secret plan' to remove PM Pashinyan from power.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Expect Russia to continue using targeted trade restrictions as its primary pressure tool against Yerevan's Western pivot rather than direct security action, while Karapetyan's rhetoric signals continued Russian-aligned opposition activity.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 21 Jul — Berlin: Aliyev signed a strategic partnership agreement with Germany covering energy, transport, infrastructure, trade and science, and confirmed a 10-year gas supply contract.
Ongoing since 13 Jul — Baku: Azerbaijan continues weighing full withdrawal from the Council of Europe after PACE suspended its delegation's voting rights.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Expect Baku to continue leveraging its energy relationship with Europe as counterweight to the PACE dispute, using the Council of Europe threat as negotiating pressure rather than following through on withdrawal in the near term.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's El Obeid siege has escalated in line with the prior 'next El Fasher' warning, though it has not yet produced a single mass-casualty event of that scale — 15 drone strikes and at least 45 civilian deaths over three weeks, plus RSF's 27 Jul retaliatory strikes on municipal buildings after SAF's highway recapture, mark the region's clearest near-term mass-atrocity risk.

Mali's FLA-JNIM cooperation has shifted from tactical to structural, formalized via a pact trading FLA acceptance of sharia governance for JNIM military backing — described this week as pushing the northern conflict into a 'dangerous new phase,' compounded by unverified reports of Russian Africa Corps forces abandoning FAMa troops mid-ambush.

The central Sahel triangle shows sustained rather than newly escalating pressure — Niger's Tillabéri remains the primary JNIM-ISSP battleground, and Burkina Faso saw further repelled JNIM attacks, though Niger in particular has a notable reporting gap this week that should not be read as reduced risk.

Sudan-Chad border dynamics and Lake Chad Basin displacement are compounding regional spillover risk — SAF and RSF are both reinforcing toward the Chad border while Boko Haram/JAS factions reposition in Lake Province, and Mauritania's 144 dead/missing Atlantic migration disaster remains the region's deadliest humanitarian incident of 2026.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 21-22 Jul — Anefis/Tabankort: Reporting alleged Russia's Africa Corps personnel retreated rather than reinforcing the besieged FAMa convoy during the 18 Jul ambush, fueling Bamako-Moscow recrimination over the loss of 50+ soldiers.

22 Jul — Northern Mali: Analysts confirmed the FLA-JNIM alliance is a formalized pact — the Azawad Liberation Front accepted sharia governance in exchange for JNIM military backing against the Bamako junta.

27 Jul — Northern Mali: Analysts described the conflict as entering a 'dangerous new phase,' detailing a six-day siege of FAMa-Africa Corps positions at Anefis following the 4 Jul coordinated attack wave.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect continued FLA-JNIM coordinated pressure on FAMa-Africa Corps positions in the Kidal-Anefis-Gao corridor, with the newly formalized alliance structure suggesting sustained rather than opportunistic cooperation; watch for further Russia-Mali friction over the Africa Corps 'abandonment' narrative and potential extension of FLA-JNIM coordination toward Niger's Tillabéri corridor.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 17 Jul — Téra, Tillabéri region: 16 Nigerien soldiers were killed and 23 wounded in a militant attack near the tri-border zone; authorities reported 15 attackers killed.
Ongoing through Jul — Tillabéri: ACLED confirmed the region remains the principal JNIM-ISSP competitive battleground, with both groups intensifying attacks to expand territorial control.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No new discrete incident was confirmed within the 21-28 July window specifically — flagged as a reporting gap rather than reduced violence. Tillabéri remains the most contested ground in the central Sahel, with JNIM-ISSP rivalry likely to drive further attacks on military and civilian targets independent of external triggers.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 19-20 Jul — Djibo, Sahel region: A large-scale JNIM assault on Burkinabè defense and security force positions was repelled, per state media.
21-27 Jul — Soum region: A JNIM attempt to storm Burkinabè armed forces positions was repelled, per lower-confidence single-source reporting pending independent corroboration.
22-23 Jul — Eastern Burkina Faso: A jihadist attack on a settlement killed both military personnel and civilians and burned homes, per lower-confidence single-source reporting.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Confidence in this week's specific incident data is lower than for other Sahel states due to reliance on a single aggregator source; recommend independent corroboration. Broader trend of sustained JNIM pressure across the Sahel, North and East regions, in competition with ISSP, continues unchanged.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 21 Jul — Tine, North Darfur: A drone strike on a water source killed at least 21 civilians.

21-22 Jul — North Darfur: SAF sent major reinforcements to Tine, Um Baru, Karnoi and Kulbus/Jebel Moon, with RSF and the Joint Force also reinforcing near the Chad border, raising fears of renewed fighting.

Documented over a 3-week span through ~20 Jul — El Obeid: The UN recorded 15 drone strikes killing at least 45 civilians, with investigators warning RSF is replicating the El Fasher siege pattern — infrastructure attacks, sieges and restricted essential services.
27 Jul — El Obeid: RSF drone strikes hit two municipal buildings hours after SAF regained control of the highway to Khartoum, assessed as retaliatory.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. El Obeid's siege pattern is intensifying in line with the prior warning of a repeat El Fasher-scale atrocity — 15 drone strikes and 45+ civilian deaths over three weeks, continued infrastructure targeting, and immediate RSF retaliation for SAF's highway recapture — though no single mass-casualty event of El Fasher's scale has yet occurred. El Obeid remains the highest-probability mass-atrocity flashpoint in the region; SAF/RSF reinforcement near the Chad border also raises direct spillover risk within the 90-day horizon.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 21-22 Jul — Chad-Sudan border: SAF, the Joint Force and RSF reinforced positions along the border near Tine, Um Baru, Karnoi, Kulbus and Jebel Moon, raising direct spillover risk for eastern Chad.

21 Jul — Lake Chad: Video evidence showed Boko Haram (JAS) fighters relocating families and camps amid intensified Nigerian and Chadian military pressure, consistent with warnings of a resurgence attempt in Lake Province.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No single new discrete attack inside Chad was confirmed this week, but rising risk is building from both directions — SAF/RSF reinforcement toward the Chad border and Boko Haram repositioning in Lake Province — either of which could produce a triggering incident within the 90-day horizon.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 18 Jul — Off Nouadhibou: A vessel that departed The Gambia with roughly 180 people spent 25 days at sea; only 38 survivors were rescued, with 1 body recovered.

Reported 21-22 Jul (UNHCR) — Off Nouadhibou: 144 refugees and migrants were confirmed dead or missing across a series of incidents, confirmed by UNHCR, IOM and MSF as the deadliest 2026 Atlantic migration-route incident.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Continued high-profile UN, IOM and MSF statements this week indicate sustained international attention on Mauritania's coast guard and rescue capacity as the primary departure point on the world's deadliest migration route.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 20-21 Jul — Sokoto/Zamfara: Operation Fansan Yamma rescued 27 kidnap victims in coordinated actions along the Gummi-Sokoto road and surrounding areas.

25 Jul — Zamfara: Bandits abducted the Bungudu LGA chairman from his residence, killing 2 police officers and 2 vigilantes; 4-5 abducted family members were later rescued but the chairman remains in captivity.

27 Jul — Borno: Troops of Operation Hadin Kai foiled an ISWAP/JAS infiltration attempt on Forward Operating Base Logomani and evacuated 21 female students from Monguno after intelligence indicated armed operatives carrying IEDs near an IDP camp.
Ongoing — Lassa, Borno: 36 students and 1 staff member abducted on 30 Jun remain in captivity, with no verified release this window.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Zamfara/Sokoto bandit activity and Borno ISWAP/JAS pressure both continue at high tempo, with active countermeasures achieving partial rescues but not eliminating abduction risk — bandits remain willing to target local government officials directly. The Lassa captives remain the priority unresolved hostage situation.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: South China Sea escalation has crossed a frequency threshold — a single unprecedented melee at Second Thomas Shoal on 20 Jul became a sustained pattern of at least four physical China-Philippines confrontations within one week at both Second Thomas and Scarborough Shoals, prompting the Philippines' elevation to CRITICAL.

Taiwan Strait gray-zone activity is diversifying beyond ship and aircraft sortie counts — the 21 Jul coordinated PLA helicopter-drone median-line crossing followed by two days of live-fire drills demonstrates Beijing experimenting with new incursion modalities ahead of Taiwan's Han Kuang exercise (5-14 Aug).

Two governments openly reconsidered nuclear postures this week in opposite directions — Japan's Defense Minister called for breaking the nuclear-weapons-debate taboo while North Korea's Kim Yo Jong doubled down on rejecting denuclearization, indicating the regional nuclear-restraint architecture is under strain from both a treaty ally and the primary proliferator.

Civil conflict and internal-security fronts in Myanmar, Pakistan and Indonesia show no sign of abating despite parallel political processes, suggesting electoral and political milestones in fragile states are not translating into reduced kinetic activity.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 16-17 Jul — DMZ area: Satellite imagery confirmed at least 21 identical drive-through structures near bases south of Kaesong, 52km from Seoul, assessed as TEL/MLRS maintenance and storage infrastructure.
22 Jul — Manila: US, Japanese and South Korean foreign ministers held trilateral talks reaffirming a 'robust deterrence posture' against North Korea.

26 Jul — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong denounced renewed denuclearization calls, calling North Korea's nuclear arsenal its 'ultimate shield,' coinciding with warnings of additional DPRK troop deployments to Russia.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. North Korea will continue hardening frontline precision-strike infrastructure along the DMZ while publicly foreclosing denuclearization diplomacy. Expect continued trilateral US-ROK-Japan coordination but no direct crisis trigger in the near term; monitor for missile tests timed to regional exercises and continued satellite-confirmed infrastructure buildout.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 19 Jul — Ma-Ei, Taungup Township, Rakhine: A junta fighter jet dropped bombs killing 5 civilians and injuring 14, including a monk and three children.
19-20 Jul — Sagaing Region: A paramotor strike killed 9 civilians, including 2 children, and destroyed 25+ homes and a church.
21 Jul — Paletwa Township, Chin State: An artillery exchange during Tatmadaw-Arakan Army fighting killed a civilian woman between Meeletwa and Yokewa villages.
Cumulative — Nationwide: The verified toll from airstrikes reached 274 civilian deaths since 20 April 2026, with researchers separately recording 450+ civilian deaths from mass killings in H1 2026.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No de-escalation indicators despite the junta's rhetoric of a '100-day ultimatum' for talks; airstrike and drone-attack tempo against AA/EAO-held territory in Rakhine, Sagaing and Chin States remains sustained to intense, with continued mass-casualty events tied to contested resource corridors.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 21-24 Jul — Azad Kashmir: The JAAC long march remained suspended pending negotiations with the Army Chief's office; internet service partially restored in Mirpur/AJK after a 48-day blackout.

27 Jul — Mirpur Division, AJK: The first phase of a staggered general election was held under heavy security — 17,000+ personnel plus ~2,100 Army troops — against a backdrop of 30-40 protest-related deaths since June.
Ongoing — Balochistan: Operation Shaban's toll continued climbing, reaching 139 militants killed since 5 July, including 2 female suicide bombers apprehended before detonation.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The staggered, three-phase AJK election design reflects a state assessment that simultaneous polling posed unacceptable security risk; expect comparable heavy-security postures for the remaining phases (2 and 10 Aug). Operation Shaban will likely continue as a grinding counter-insurgency campaign without a clear end-state.

countries.name: India
incidents: 17 Jul — Chandel district, Manipur: KYKL cadre Yangabam Boicha Meitei was arrested near the Indo-Myanmar border with a pistol and communications equipment.
19-20 Jul — Chakpikarong PS, Chandel: Three KYKL cadres were arrested near the border.
24-26 Jul — Manipur: Additional militant cadres and drug peddlers were arrested in separate security-force crackdowns, with arms and drugs caches recovered.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Steady-state counter-insurgency arrests continue along the Indo-Myanmar border in Manipur's Chandel/Ukhrul belt, with no mass-casualty incident this week — a continuation rather than escalation of the established pattern; narco-insurgency overlap suggests security forces are prioritizing interdiction of cross-border logistics.

countries.name: China
incidents: 21 Jul — Taiwan Strait: A PLA helicopter and drone jointly crossed the median line and lingered in the restricted zone for roughly 9.5 hours, the first coordinated helicopter-drone incursion of this duration.
23-24 Jul — Fujian coast: The PLA conducted a two-day live-fire drill in the Strait after Beijing labeled Taiwan President Lai's recent speech 'reckless.'

20, 23-25 Jul — South China Sea: Chinese coast guard/maritime forces were involved in a physical melee with Philippine Navy personnel at Second Thomas Shoal and three separate water-cannon or dangerous-maneuver incidents near Scarborough Shoal within a single week.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, trending toward the top of the band. Beijing is layering simultaneous gray-zone pressure on two fronts — sustained median-line normalization near Taiwan and intensified multi-incident-per-week coercion against the Philippines — ahead of Taiwan's Han Kuang exercise. Expect continued incremental median-line crossings and further live-fire drills timed to Taiwanese political statements.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 21 Jul — Taiwan Strait: The first coordinated PLA helicopter/drone incursion east of the median line lingered roughly 9.5 hours in the restricted R9 zone.
23-24 Jul — Off Fujian: The PLA conducted a two-day live-fire drill in response to President Lai's speech.
24-28 Jul — Keelung: An Nvidia employee was detained as Taiwan's AI-chip smuggling investigation expanded, following the earlier Super Micro Taiwan raid.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Taipei faces a two-track pressure campaign — external gray-zone military normalization and internal legislative friction over defense funding — heading into Han Kuang Exercise No. 42 (5-14 Aug), which will simulate PLA drills concealing invasion preparation. Recommend close monitoring of Han Kuang execution against the backdrop of intensified median-line activity.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 20 Jul — Second Thomas Shoal: Chinese Coast Guard personnel rammed and exchanged blows with Philippine Navy crew near the Sierra Madre — the first confirmed direct physical violence in the dispute, injuring a servicemember.

23 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: China fired water cannon at a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries vessel for over 2 minutes, while a second Chinese vessel conducted a dangerous maneuver against a Philippine resupply boat.
24 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: A Chinese vessel fired water cannon at a Philippine ship carrying a CNN crew, the third faceoff in a single week.
25 Jul — Scarborough Shoal: A Chinese coast guard vessel approached a Philippine fisheries ship within 7 meters in a 'reckless' near-collision maneuver.
countries.coa: Upgraded to CRITICAL from HIGH. What was flagged last week as a singular first-of-its-kind melee proved to be the opening incident in a sustained pattern — four physical confrontations in six days, an unprecedented frequency, with the US Embassy in Manila publicly condemning China's 'escalatory' actions. Expect continued high-frequency coast guard and maritime militia harassment at both shoals, with elevated risk of a further physical-injury incident; watch for a US Mutual Defense Treaty invocation threshold being tested if a Philippine service member is killed or a vessel is sunk.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: Ongoing through Jul — Nationwide: The Kimsuky (APT43) group conducted a spear-phishing campaign against a South Korean military organization using AI-generated deepfake images of military ID cards.
22 Jul — Manila: South Korea joined the trilateral foreign ministers' meeting reaffirming deterrence posture against North Korea.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Kimsuky's use of generative-AI-crafted deepfake credentials marks a tactical evolution in North Korean cyber-espionage tradecraft targeting South Korea's defense-industrial base; expect continued targeting of software vendors and defense-adjacent contractors.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 19 Jul (carried over) — South China Sea: Vietnam continued to press its accusation that the Chinese survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi 8 and its escorts violated its EEZ and continental shelf.

11 Jul — International: 14 countries marked the 10th anniversary of the Hague Tribunal ruling against China's South China Sea claims with a joint statement; Vietnam notably did not co-sign, consistent with its bilateral-management approach.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; sparse new reporting this window. Vietnam likely continues its established pattern of quiet diplomatic protest over public confrontation regarding Chinese survey and EEZ activity; recommend re-verification of the Haiyang Dizhi 8 situation in the next cycle given the gap in fresh sourcing.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 19-23 Jul — Tokyo: Defense Minister Shinjirō Koizumi stated Japan 'cannot avoid' a nuclear weapons debate and doubled down on 'breaking the taboo,' citing North Korea's missile program and China's military presence.

Ongoing — Tokyo: PM Takaichi confirmed intent to discuss revising Japan's three security documents, including its non-nuclear principles, alongside the Japan Innovation Party's separate push for nuclear-submarine acquisition.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, watch for upgrade. This is a significant political escalation rather than a kinetic one — a sitting Defense Minister openly inviting debate on nuclear weapons is unprecedented for postwar Japan. No new Senkaku incident was found this week beyond the previously reported faceoff; expect continued domestic political maneuvering around the security-document revision process.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 21 Jul — Yahukimo Regency, Papua: TPNPB-OPM fighters shot and killed three Indigenous civilians, alleging they were military intelligence informants; Indonesian authorities rejected the claim.
Ongoing — Papua: TNI continued reinforcing 'vulnerable' locations following the 2 Jul killing of an American pilot at Balinggama airstrip, Yahukimo.
5 Jul (carried over) — Papua: A centralized drone command center for Papua operations was inaugurated, alongside plans for two new territorial military commands in Nabire and Sorong.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The 21 Jul Yahukimo killings, following the earlier security operation and the pilot killing, indicate the Trans Papua road corridor remains the epicenter of TPNPB-OPM activity, with TNI responding via permanent infrastructure buildup rather than only reactive deployments, signaling a shift toward sustained militarization.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 24 Jul — Nationwide: PM Anutin Charnvirakul marked the first anniversary of the July 2025 border conflict, stating there was 'nothing to celebrate' while affirming the security situation 'has returned to normal.'

Ongoing — Border area: More than 20,000 displaced Cambodians remain unable to return home due to continued Thai military presence in contested territory, and the border crossing remains officially closed.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The ceasefire holds structurally but the PM's own 'no cause for celebration' rhetoric signals persistent underlying friction; displacement and border closure issues remain unresolved political liabilities for both governments. No new kinetic incident was found this window.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 22 Jul (carried over) — Dhaka: The BNP publicly distanced itself from the July National Charter-backed reform agenda, deepening its rift with the NCP and Jamaat over constitutional reform implementation.
6-7 Jul (carried over) — Savar: A crude-bomb attack on an NCP rally injured 4, consistent with the pattern of low-level political violence.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; sparse new reporting this window. Absent new incident data, the underlying trend of persistent low-level political violence under the BNP government likely continues, with the widening BNP-NCP/Jamaat rift over constitutional reform likely to generate further public friction.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: Ongoing — Nationwide: The Human Rights Commission's investigation into the Negombo prison violence (25-28 dead, 100+ injured) expanded to cover subsequent incidents, including denial of access during an unannounced visit to Welikada Prison.

Ongoing — Nationwide: Torture allegations regarding transferred inmates remain under UN and Amnesty International scrutiny; overcrowding was cited as a root cause, with Negombo Prison (built for ~640) holding roughly 2,400 inmates.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The Human Rights Commission's expanded, multi-facility investigation suggests findings will extend beyond Negombo itself. Expect a formal report within the 90-day horizon, with continued international pressure in parallel; risk of further unrest is elevated if the investigation stalls.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Two simultaneous constitutional crises are converging on early August — Colombia's 7 Aug inauguration remains venue-undefined with Petro actively obstructing preparations, while Venezuela saw dueling nationwide mobilizations on 28 Jul testing the durability of the interim order.

Peru's power transfer completed successfully with Keiko Fujimori's 28 Jul inauguration, but inherits an unresolved extortion and sicariato crisis that her mega-prison agenda cannot address on a timescale shorter than several months.

Infrastructure and governance fragility, not conventional conflict, remain the dominant driver of instability in the Caribbean — Cuba's grid-collapse-driven protest wave continues spreading geographically, and Haiti's Gang Suppression Force has effectively conceded it cannot meet its original timeline.

Economic stabilization is quietly outpacing political crisis in the Andean periphery — Bolivia's IMF deal is close to finalized with unrest sharply down since June, while Ecuador has shifted from emergency-footing to institutionalizing militarized counter-gang policy through 2029.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 26-27 Jul — Nationwide: María Corina Machado's opposition called simultaneous assemblies in all 335 municipalities for 28 Jul, while competing Chavista-aligned coalitions convened rival marches in Caracas for the same date.
27 Jul — Caracas: Venezuela formally notified the UN of its withdrawal from the Rome Statute/ICC, calling the move 'firm and irrevocable.'

27 Jul — Nationwide: One month after the late-June earthquakes, the UN launched a roughly $300 million appeal for survivors, with tens of thousands still unaccounted for and warnings of an impending health crisis in overcrowded shelters.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. No single decisive event, but converging pressure points — the 28 Jul dueling mobilizations, ICC withdrawal, and earthquake humanitarian strain — sustain elevated risk. Expect the mobilizations to pass without decisive rupture but to harden factional lines between the interim government, the Machado-aligned opposition and residual Chavista structures; the ICC exit removes a legal accountability lever and should be read alongside continued US-Venezuela alignment on oil-sector restructuring. The earthquake recovery will remain a chronic drag on governability through October.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 19 Jul — Kapenyen, Artibonite: A Kokorat San Ras gang attack killed at least 7 and injured about 10 in this anti-gang resistance stronghold.
20 Jul — UN Headquarters: The UN Special Representative briefed the Security Council on Gang Suppression Force progress; deployment remains at roughly 1,000 of the 5,550 authorized personnel.
22 Jul — Haiti: GSF leadership requested a two-year mandate extension through 2028, an implicit admission that near-term benchmarks will not be met.
Ongoing — Nationwide: Armed groups now control an estimated 85% of the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area, with over 2,000 killed and roughly 1.5 million displaced since January 2026.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The GSF's request for a two-year extension, made just months into deployment, is itself a significant signal the mission is falling well short of pace. Absent a substantial and rapid increase in troop contributions (currently ~18% of authorized strength), expect continued gang territorial consolidation in Port-au-Prince and further incursions into Artibonite, Centre and the Kenscoff/Grand Fond corridor.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 21 Jul — Bogotá: Gustavo Petro filed a lawsuit seeking annulment of Abelardo de la Espriella's electoral victory proclamation, alleging degraded controls over electoral forms.

Mid-late Jul — Bogotá: Petro barred any military garrison or police facility from being used for the 7 Aug inauguration; the Senate voted to move the site to Cauca department, while De la Espriella's team reportedly sought Cali instead — the venue remained formally undefined as of 27 Jul.

14 Jul (carried over) — Chocó: In the wake of the 39-hostage ELN abduction/rescue, the ELN unleashed a wave of 50+ violent actions over six days, with over 50,000 residents effectively confined by armed groups fighting for territorial control.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The inauguration-venue standoff is now a live constitutional crisis with the 7 Aug transfer date essentially unresolved with under two weeks to go. Expect a real risk of a contested or dual-track inauguration, with legal challenges and heightened potential for street mobilization by both camps; ELN/Clan del Golfo violence in Chocó will likely persist regardless of who is inaugurated, reflecting a territorial dynamic largely insulated from Bogotá's political turmoil.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 18-19 Jul — Havana (Lawton, San Agustín, La Coronela, La Lisa) and Santiago de Cuba, Cienfuegos: Pot-banging protests continued and spread, with chants of 'Freedom' and 'We want the light.'
25 Jul — Nationwide: Widespread daily outages persisted following the three total grid collapses of early-to-mid July.
26 Jul — Havana: State TV aired a broadcast timed to the Moncada Barracks anniversary intended to preempt protest activity; pot-banging protests continued regardless in multiple Havana neighborhoods.
25-27 Jul — Santiago de Cuba: At least one youth was detained following a protest, triggering a further wave of neighbors leaving their homes in response.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, now the largest sustained protest wave since July 2021 and still spreading geographically. Expect localized pot-banging protests to continue and likely intensify through hurricane season, which further stresses the fragile grid, punctuated by periodic total or partial collapses; government response will likely continue to rely on targeted arrests rather than systemic fixes.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 20 Jul — Manta, La Revancha: Two armed men shot at a resident inside a home; two suspected sicarios were later detained.
25 Jul — Manta: A motorcyclist was shot dead in broad daylight, pushing the Manta-Montecristi-Jaramijó district's 2026 violent-death toll to 292.

28 Jul — Portoviejo, Riochico: A man was shot dead, bringing Portoviejo's separate 2026 death toll to 134; ACLED confirmed June was Manabí province's worst month for organized-crime violence since 2022.
Mid-Jul — Nationwide: A third executive decree locked the militarized state-of-exception strategy in place as official policy through 2029, beyond the current 60-day emergency window.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Manabí will likely remain Ecuador's principal violence hotspot as the Los Choneros-Los Lobos dispute over trafficking routes continues unresolved. The decision to institutionalize the militarized strategy through 2029 signals recognition that this is now a chronic rather than emergency-phase conflict, raising the likelihood of normalized elevated violence rather than either escalation or meaningful de-escalation.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 22 Jul — Lima: President-elect Fujimori formally called for Bukele-style CECOT-modeled mega-prisons, alongside anonymous judges for criminal trials and mandatory prison labor.
22 Jul — Lima, Carabayllo corridor: A bicycle-borne sicario executed a combi driver, intensifying fear across the public transport sector.
27 Jul — Lima: Relatives of victims of state violence under Alberto Fujimori protested on the eve of Keiko Fujimori's inauguration, rejecting her government.

28 Jul — Lima: Keiko Fujimori was sworn in as Peru's first elected female president after her narrow runoff win, pledging an 'iron fist' security agenda; her party holds the largest but not a majority congressional bloc.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The inauguration proceeded without major disruption, but the extortion/sicariato crisis driving her mandate is unresolved and her security agenda is not yet implemented — a seven-month mega-prison construction timeline is unlikely to affect the extortion economy before Q4 2026 at the earliest. Expect continued transport-sector killings and extortion-linked violence in Lima/Callao at or near the current pace, alongside potential friction with human-rights and victims' groups.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 22 Jul — La Paz: The Economy Minister confirmed Bolivia is 'days away' from a $2.5-2.8 billion IMF financing agreement, with over half the funds arriving by early September for central bank reserve reinforcement.

Ongoing — El Alto/Chonchocoro: Túpac Katari farmers'-federation leader Vicente Salazar remains in pretrial detention on terrorism-related charges tied to the blockade campaign, with a habeas corpus petition still pending.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The IMF agreement, if finalized as expected, should ease near-term FX and reserve pressure and support continued de-escalation of nationwide demonstrations, which have already dropped sharply since May. The Salazar case remains a latent risk: an adverse ruling or extended detention could reactivate the farmers'-federation mobilization base.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 24-25 Jul — Enriquillo, Barahona: Authorities detained two Dominican nationals transporting 11 undocumented Haitians by bus on human-trafficking charges, illustrative of routine enforcement activity.
Ongoing (June data) — Nationwide: 34,226 Haitians were deported in June alone, consistent with the roughly 10,000/week pace.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. No new dated escalatory incidents were found this window; the deportation campaign continues at its established pace absent a policy announcement change.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: Data through mid-Jul — Nationwide: 288-291 murders were recorded year-to-date, 22-24% below the same period last year, with the murder clearance rate at 111% versus 71% a year earlier.
June data — Nationwide: Police lethality rose sharply, with 11 suspects killed by police in a single 48-hour window, prompting community protests and roadblocks in Montego Bay.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The murder-reduction trend is expected to continue absent a major disruptive event. The main watch item is not organized crime but police-community relations: continued high police-lethality rates could catalyze further localized unrest even as overall crime statistics improve.
